decision.reason: With line framing a corrupt '{' line is a lost protocol message, such as a control_response, so skipping it silently can hang a pending request. Non-JSON noise is still skipped.

Permission modes pass through untyped; unknown values are not rejected.

upstream.behavior: Exceeding the pending thresholds (500 entries, 1 MiB) triggers an eager flush; nothing is rejected.
A failed append is reported as a system mirror_error message; the run outcome is unaffected.

python.reason: Python always mirrors from the subprocess config dir and has no custom spawn hook to warn about.

typescript.anchor: ensure the subprocess CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR matches the parent

upstream.behavior: A possible mismatch is at most a warning, never an error.

rows.concept: Resume with a non-UUID session id

upstream.behavior: A non-UUID resume id skips store materialization and leaves --resume to the CLI.

rows.concept: Resume of a session with no stored entries

upstream.behavior: A missing or empty stored session materializes nothing and is not an error.
Unsafe subpaths (empty, absolute, '..', escaping the session dir) are skipped with a warning.
Two parts ending in .jsonl give a main key; four or more parts give a subpath key with .jsonl stripped.

rows.concept: Continue when the newest listed session id is not a UUID

typescript.anchor: Options.continue with sessionStore requires store.listSessions to be implemented

upstream.behavior: Python skips the candidate and tries the next newest. TypeScript takes the newest entry only, so a non-UUID newest id starts a fresh session.

decision.reason: Both rules are exposed through SessionStoreOptions.dialect. TypeScript, the default, takes only the newest listed session and starts fresh when its id is not a UUID; the Python dialect tries the next newest.

rows.concept: Unknown permission suggestion destinations, behaviors and update types

upstream.behavior: Neither SDK validates suggestion values. TypeScript passes permission_suggestions raw to canUseTool; Python accepts any string for type, destination, behavior and mode, so an unrecognized suggestion reaches the callback and round-trips verbatim into updatedPermissions.

rows.concept: Structurally malformed permission suggestions and requests

upstream.behavior: Python decodes every suggestion, so a structurally broken one (a missing type, rules that are not a list) or a missing tool_name raises inside the control handler, which answers that request with an error response while the session continues. TypeScript forwards the raw suggestions to canUseTool without decoding them, so nothing fails.

decision.reason: A typed suggestion cannot represent a broken object, so the request is answered with an error response instead of reaching the callback, and neither the session nor other requests are affected.

rows.concept: Which transcript mirror append errors are retried

upstream.behavior: Every non-timeout append error is retried, three attempts with 200 ms and 800 ms backoff.

typescript.anchor: enableFileCheckpointing is not yet supported with sessionStore

upstream.behavior: Configuring a session store together with file checkpointing is rejected before spawn.

rows.concept: Where store-backed resume transcripts are materialized

upstream.behavior: Transcripts are written to a fresh temp dir that becomes the subprocess CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, on every platform.

rows.concept: Two SDK MCP tools with the same name

upstream.behavior: TypeScript throws 'Tool <name> is already registered'. Python keeps the last handler and lists both tools.

decision.reason: A duplicate name makes tools/list and tools/call disagree in Python; rejecting at registration is the only unambiguous outcome.

typescript.anchor: Input validation error: Invalid arguments for tool

upstream.behavior: An unknown tool returns an isError tool result naming the tool, not a JSON-RPC error.

rows.concept: tools/call arguments that fail the input schema

typescript.anchor: Input validation error: Invalid arguments for tool

upstream.behavior: Invalid arguments return an isError tool result with an input validation message, not a JSON-RPC error.

rows.concept: Blocking hooks against a responder without onFailure support

typescript.anchor: does not honor onFailure on hook matchers

upstream.behavior: Initialize fails when a blocking hook is configured and hook_on_failure_supported is not true.

Python times out after 60 s with "Control request timeout: {subtype}". TypeScript waits until the response arrives, the abort signal fires, or the query closes; its only initialize deadline is 660000 ms, armed when a hook is set to block on failure or managed settings are sent.

decision.reason: Limits::control_timeout is None by default and InitializeTimeout::TypeScript arms 660 s only for blocking hooks or managed settings, failing with InitializeNotConfirmed or ManagedSettingsNotConfirmed and TypeScript's text. Limits::python() selects the 60 s wait, Python's message and the CLAUDE_CODE_STREAM_CLOSE_TIMEOUT initialize wait.

upstream.behavior: An error subtype rejects the pending request with the CLI's error message.

rows.concept: Size of one inbound stdout message

upstream.behavior: Python rejects a line over max_buffer_size (1 MiB by default) with "JSON message exceeded maximum buffer size of {N} bytes". TypeScript reads lines with node:readline and no length limit.

decision.reason: Limits::max_buffer_size is None by default; Limits::python() sets Python's 1 MiB cap with its message.

upstream.behavior: Store loads time out after 60000 ms by default.
A timed-out append is not retried because the in-flight call may still land.

rows.concept: Continue when the newest session is a sidechain

typescript.anchor: Options.continue with sessionStore requires store.listSessions to be implemented

upstream.behavior: Python walks newest to oldest and skips sessions whose first entry has isSidechain true. TypeScript resumes the newest listed session.

decision.reason: Both rules are exposed through SessionStoreOptions.dialect. TypeScript, the default, resumes the newest listed session even when it is a sidechain; the Python dialect walks past sidechains.

upstream.behavior: Non-alphanumerics become '-'; keys over 200 chars are truncated and suffixed with a base36 hash.

rows.concept: Mirror frame whose file path is outside the projects dir

upstream.behavior: The frame is dropped with a warning.

typescript.anchor: Options.continue with sessionStore requires store.listSessions to be implemented

upstream.behavior: continue without an explicit resume requires the store to implement list_sessions.

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no equivalent bound.

upstream.behavior: No queue capacity setting exists upstream. Rust queues are unbounded unless a caller opts into a bound, and an opted-in QueueCapacity still rejects zero and values past the semaphore permit limit.

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no equivalent bound.

upstream.behavior: Timeouts are not range-checked upstream. Timeout::new accepts any duration and a deadline past the clock's range never fires; Timeout::checked keeps the Zero and TooLarge errors for callers that want them.
The budget is passed to the CLI without validation: TypeScript as --max-budget-usd=${String(f)} and Python as str(value) after --max-budget-usd.

rows.concept: CLI path that is a .bat or .cmd script

typescript.reason: sdk.mjs resolves and spawns the CLI path without a batch-script guard.

upstream.behavior: Python refuses .bat and .cmd CLI paths on Windows. TypeScript spawns them.

decision.reason: WindowsBatchCli::Run is the default, so a .bat or .cmd path starts as in TypeScript; WindowsBatchCli::Refuse selects Python's refusal with its message as CliPathError::WindowsBatchScript.

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no equivalent bound.

upstream.behavior: Writes to the CLI are not time-bounded upstream; TypeScript only logs when the stdin buffer is full. Rust waits for the write unless Limits::write_timeout is set, which fails a stalled write with WriteTimeout.

rows.concept: Timeout waiting for the client command queue

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no equivalent bound.

upstream.behavior: No client command queue exists upstream. Rust's command queue is unbounded and never times out unless Limits::command_queue_capacity is set; Limits::command_queue_timeout then bounds the wait for room with CommandQueueTimeout.

TypeScript closes stdin, waits 2000 ms, sends SIGTERM (none on Windows) and SIGKILL 5000 ms later without waiting, gives stderr 200 ms after the exit, and never reports an error. Python waits 5 s, terminates, waits 5 s, kills and waits 5 s, suppressing every error.

decision.reason: Shutdown::TypeScript is the default; Limits::python() selects Shutdown::Python, and Shutdown::Strict keeps ShutdownTimeout and StderrDrainTimeout as an opt-in.

upstream.behavior: TypeScript keeps the last 2048 UTF-16 code units of stderr and appends them, trimmed, to the process error. Python keeps no stderr and reports "Check stderr output for details".

decision.reason: Limits::stderr_tail defaults to TypeScript's 2048 units; Limits::python() sets it to 0. TypeScript's secret redaction of the tail is not ported.

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no equivalent bound.

upstream.behavior: Upstream request ids are random strings that never run out. The Rust counter wraps by default so ids never run out either; RequestIdExhaustion::Fail keeps RequestIdExhausted as an opt-in.

rows.concept: Sending before initialize or after input closed

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no equivalent bound.

upstream.behavior: Upstream holds writes until initialize is sent and writes input sent after the caller ended its stream. Rust writes such input by default; InputAfterFinish::Reject keeps InputClosed as an opt-in. NotInitialized is only reachable from inside the driver, because the client returns only after initialize succeeds.

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no equivalent bound.

upstream.behavior: Outstanding control requests are unbounded upstream. Limits::max_pending_controls is opt-in and fails the excess request with TooManyControls.

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no equivalent bound.

upstream.behavior: Inbound callbacks are unbounded upstream. Limits::max_incoming_callbacks is opt-in and answers the excess request with an error response.
TypeScript queues messages in an unbounded array and keeps reading stdout. Python buffers 100 messages and then stops reading until the caller takes one.

decision.reason: MessageBuffer::Unbounded is the default; Limits::python() selects MessageBuffer::Backpressure(100), and MessageBuffer::FailWhenFull keeps MessageQueueFull as an opt-in.

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no equivalent bound.

upstream.behavior: Tracked tasks are unbounded upstream. Limits::max_tracked_tasks is opt-in and fails the run with TooManyTasks.

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no equivalent bound.

upstream.behavior: Queued prompts are unbounded upstream. Limits::max_queued_inputs is opt-in and fails with TooManyInputs.

rows.concept: Inbound control_request with a duplicate id

upstream.behavior: TypeScript skips an inbound request whose id is still in flight, with a debug log and no response. Python runs both handlers and both answer.

decision.reason: DuplicateControlRequests::Skip is the default; Limits::python() selects RunBoth, and DuplicateControlRequests::Fail keeps DuplicateControlRequest as an opt-in.

python.reason: Python keeps one mcp_servers dict, so a name holds one config.

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no equivalent bound.

upstream.behavior: The final flush is not separately bounded upstream. Rust waits for the flush by default, each append still bounded by append_timeout; SessionStoreLimits::flush_timeout opts into a deadline that fails with MirrorFlushTimeout.

upstream.behavior: Upstream keeps no failure records and reports every failed append. Rust reports every failure by default; SessionStoreLimits::max_retained_failures opts into a cap that folds the overflow into one Suppressed failure.
Python always sends the matcher key and sends null when no matcher is set. TypeScript sends the key as undefined, which JSON serialization drops, so the registration has no matcher key.

decision.reason: TypeScript is the default dialect and declares matcher as an optional string, so the key is omitted; ArgvStyle::Python sends null.

rows.concept: User dialog request that no handler answers

upstream.behavior: Python has no user dialog support, so the request reaches its unsupported subtype branch and is answered with an error response. TypeScript with no handler, or a handler that returns null, deliberately sends no response so a capable client can answer.

decision.reason: An answer from this client would pre-empt another client that can show the dialog, and an error would end the dialog for the user. The session continues without a response.

rows.concept: Bundled Claude Code executable beside the Python package

typescript.reason: sdk.mjs resolves a platform package instead of a bundled directory.

upstream.behavior: Python checks <package>/_bundled/claude (claude.exe on Windows) before any other discovery and accepts it only when it exists and is a file.

decision.reason: A Rust crate ships no binary and has no package directory, so find_bundled_cli takes the directory that holds _bundled from the caller and is not part of connect's discovery.

rows.concept: Native executable from the platform optional dependency package

python.reason: The pinned Python sources bundle the binary in the wheel and never resolve npm packages.

upstream.behavior: TypeScript resolves <package>-<platform>-<arch>/claude (claude.exe on win32) through Node module resolution, tries the musl variant first on musl Linux and the glibc one first otherwise, uses a dedicated linux-<arch>-android package for Android, skips a candidate whose resolution throws or whose file is missing, and fails with a message naming the platform when none is found.

decision.reason: Node module resolution is a ResolveNodeModule adapter with a default that searches the same relative node_modules, NODE_PATH and home or prefix directories. Musl is read from the compile target because a Rust process has no Node process report.

rows.concept: Minimum version a bundled Claude Code record must meet to derive an app label

typescript.reason: sdk.mjs has no derived client app minimum and reads no version record.

upstream.behavior: The recorded version must start with major.minor.patch (up to nine digits each) and that triple, compared as a list, must not be below 999.0.0 (DERIVED_CLIENT_APP_MINIMUM_CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION). Nothing qualifies until upstream lowers the minimum.

rows.concept: Bundled Claude Code executable as the trigger for a derived client app label

typescript.reason: sdk.mjs derives no client app label from the executable that it spawns.

upstream.behavior: A label is derived only when the SDK package pin (__cli_version__) meets the minimum, the spawned CLI is the bundled executable, and the claude.version file beside it records a version that meets the minimum. Any other CLI counts as too old, a bundled one with no readable record does too, and a failure to read never breaks connect.

decision.reason: bundled_cli_derives_client_app answers the trigger for a caller-supplied package root and pin, because a Rust crate has no package directory or __cli_version__. connect asks it only when ClaudeAgentOptions::client_app_derivation names a BundledCli, so TypeScript's behavior stays the default, and the label names this crate because Rust has no Python distribution metadata.

rows.concept: Outbound control request id and envelope

upstream.behavior: TypeScript sends Math.random().toString(36).substring(2,15) with no counter, in a compact envelope that starts with request_id. Python sends req_{counter}_{8 hex digits} in an envelope that starts with type, written by json.dumps with spaced separators and ASCII escapes.

decision.reason: TypeScript is the default dialect; ArgvStyle::Python selects the Python id, envelope order and json.dumps spelling.

rows.concept: Initialize request fields and hook matcher entries

upstream.behavior: TypeScript omits hooks when none are configured, omits an unset matcher, and sends jsonSchema, systemPrompt, appendSystemPrompt and supportedDialogKinds in the request. Python sends hooks null when none are configured, matcher null when unset, and none of those prompt or schema fields. Both skip events with no matchers and keep matchers with no callbacks.

decision.reason: TypeScript is the default dialect; ArgvStyle::Python sends the Python request.

rows.concept: Initialize response that is not the documented object

upstream.behavior: Neither SDK validates the initialize response. TypeScript keeps any value as the initialization result; Python replaces anything but an object with an empty object.

decision.reason: TypeScript is the default dialect; ArgvStyle::Python reads a non-object as an empty object. Typed fields of an unexpected type read as absent and the response stays available unchanged.

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no user dialog support.

upstream.behavior: TypeScript refuses non-empty dialog kinds without a handler before the session starts.

rows.concept: Initialize response for managed settings and plugins sent in initialize

python.reason: The pinned Python sources do not send managed settings or plugins in initialize.

upstream.behavior: TypeScript ends the session when managed settings were sent and managed_settings_applied is not true, and logs a warning when plugins were sent and plugins_applied is not true.

rows.concept: Messages that are unknown, malformed or missing required keys

upstream.behavior: TypeScript yields every message the CLI writes without validating it, consuming only keep_alive and host-only session_state_changed. Python parse_message raises MessageParseError with a KeyError text for a known message missing a key it reads, skips unknown message types and skips content blocks of kinds it does not parse.

decision.reason: TypeScript is the default and never loses a message, so newer CLI shapes still reach the caller. MessageDecoding::Python reproduces parse_message, error texts included, for callers that need Python's outcome.

rows.concept: Where the system prompt travels and which forms it takes

upstream.behavior: TypeScript sends the prompt in the initialize request (systemPrompt as a list, appendSystemPrompt, systemPromptSnapshot, excludeDynamicSections) and has no prompt flag. Python puts the prompt on the command line (--system-prompt, --system-prompt-file, --append-system-prompt) and sends only excludeDynamicSections and systemPromptSnapshot in the request.

decision.reason: TypeScript is the default dialect. ClaudeAgentOptions::argv_style = ArgvStyle::Python selects Python's argv and request, and the prompt forms that exist in only one SDK (a list of texts, a prompt file) are refused in the other dialect instead of being dropped.

rows.concept: workspaceTrust with an accepted trust and no absolute directory

python.reason: claude_agent_sdk has no workspace trust option.

upstream.behavior: An accepted trust needs a directory that is absolute on posix or win32; otherwise the whole value is dropped with a warning. A declined or empty trust passes through as given.

rows.concept: Marking user messages client_composed so the CLI skips @path expansion and slash commands

upstream.behavior: With the option on, every outgoing user message carries client_composed:true after its other keys. Python additionally warns at the first init message when the CLI is older than 2.1.248 or reports no version.

rows.concept: error_code on a control error response

upstream.behavior: TypeScript keeps a string error_code matching /^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$/ as errorCode and drops any other; Python raises with the message only.

decision.reason: ControlRejectionError::error_code reads it the TypeScript way by default; ArgvStyle::Python leaves it unset like Python.

rows.concept: Control responses returned to the caller

upstream.behavior: Neither SDK validates a control response. TypeScript returns the response as sent, undefined when absent; Python returns it when it is an object and an empty object otherwise.

decision.reason: ControlReply keeps the response as sent, None when absent, and decodes it to the pinned type only on request; ArgvStyle::Python reads a missing or non-object response as an empty object.

upstream.behavior: TypeScript setModel() leaves model out of the request; Python set_model(None) sends model null.

decision.reason: set_model(None) leaves model out by default and sends null under ArgvStyle::Python.

upstream.behavior: TypeScript sends dry_run as the caller's dryRun, left out when unset; Python sends only user_message_id.

decision.reason: rewind_files(id, None) sends what both SDKs send without the option; RewindMode::DryRun and RewindMode::Apply send the TypeScript flag.

python.reason: The pinned Python client has no supported commands accessor.

upstream.behavior: supportedCommands returns the commands of the last system commands_changed message whose commands is an array, else the initialize commands.

python.reason: The pinned Python client has no reinitialize.

upstream.behavior: reinitialize sends the initialize request again without SDK MCP server manifests and returns its response; initializationResult keeps the first response.

python.reason: The pinned Python client has no background_tasks control.

upstream.behavior: backgroundTasks returns response.backgrounded, true when it is null or absent, and throws when the response itself is absent.

decision.reason: A backgrounded that is not a boolean is a protocol error, where TypeScript returns the value untyped.

python.reason: The pinned Python client has no read_file control.

upstream.behavior: readFile resolves to null on any failure, the CLI's refusal included, and leaves max_bytes and encoding out when unset.

python.reason: Python writes its own json.dumps spelling, covered by the Python dialect.

upstream.behavior: Requests are written with JSON.stringify: integral numbers without a fraction, 1e21 as 1e+21, NaN and the infinities as null.
